claim: The /contact and /sample forms submit to the shared inquiries backend in BOTH locales
evidence_source: Found broken on 2026-09-06: the English /contact and /sample forms had no submit handler of any kind. Their markup was complete - every field, every id, the honeypot, the status element, the submit button - and no script was ever bound to them. The form carries no action, so pressing Send did a default submission that reloaded the page and discarded everything the buyer had typed: no POST, no error, no trace. The Arabic pages carried a working copy of the handler inline, which is why nothing showed it. Fixed by extracting one shared handler (assets/inquiry-form.js) used by all four pages, and removing the Arabic inline copies so nothing submits twice. Verified in a real browser: all four now produce exactly one POST carrying the required fields, show a confirmation in the page's own language, and reset. scripts/check-inquiry-forms.js fails if any inquiry page loses the handler, keeps a second inline copy, renames an id the handler reads, or positions a honeypot on the wrong side for its writing direction.

claim: Six labelled inquiry entry points, all routing into backends that already exist, with the intent recorded against the enquiry
where_it_appears: /contact and /ar/contact ("What do you need?" block and the intent badge); the private-label tile routes to /resources/private-label#brief
evidence_source: No new form and no new backend. Five entry points land on the existing /contact form with ?intent= set, which the shared handler resolves to the request_type column that already existed and is already shown in the admin inquiry list and its CSV export. The sixth, private label, routes to the purpose-built brief, which captures target market, packaging, volume, certifications and Incoterm - the general form would collect less. Local Egyptian pricing routes to the general form with a local-buyer request_type because the local-market Solutions path named in the brief does not exist on this site; confirmed by checking for the route rather than assuming. Intents are a closed set: anything unrecognised falls back to the default rather than writing an arbitrary string, verified against nonsense, path traversal and a SQL-injection string. A visible badge tells the visitor which label their enquiry arrived with.
action_required: Owner to confirm whether a local-market Solutions section is still planned, which would give local pricing its own destination
